newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil key soybean states see rain, more forecast.
newsitem.headline: Brazil key soybean states see rain, more forecast.

text.p: Brazil's southern soybean growing region saw heavy rains in the week to Oct 14, principally in the key states of Rio Grande do Sul and Parana, said independent forecasters Somar Meteorologia.
In the center-west, rainfall was more irregular, mainly in Mato Grosso, it added.
In Rio Grande do Sul, towns in key soybean producing regions saw rainfall of between 56 millimeters in Santa Maria to 126 millimeters in Sao Luiz Gonzaga, well within the norm for October.
In Parana, precipitation ranged between 52 millimeters in Maringa and 70 millimeters in Londrina.
In the west, rainfall has been in excess of 100 millimeters which is above average for the time of the year.

The outlook for the week to Oct 20 is for scattered rain in the southern region. A new cold front will reach Rio Grande do Sul on October 18, bringing light showers. This system will reach Parana state by the weekend.
Temperatures will rise throughout the region.
The forecast for Mato Grosso, where soybean planting has already begun, continues for isolated showers, Somar said.
Soybean planting in Parana is likely to begin a little later than normal this year due to a delay in the wheat harvest.
As a result the main planting period in the two key states of Parana and Rio Grande do Sul will probably be November.
